added_models.model: Patient-derived primary CD138+ myeloma cells ex vivo, including cells from bortezomib-treated or bortezomib-resistant patients (Piva 2008; Chauhan 2010, 2011)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary CD138+ myeloma cells ex vivo, including cells from bortezomib-treated or bortezomib-resistant patients (Piva 2008; Chauhan 2010, 2011)
efficacy.note: CEP-18770 killed CD138+ explants from untreated and bortezomib-treated patients; ONX 0912 (2010) and MLN2238 (2011) later killed bortezomib-resistant patient cells. No patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: Bortezomib-treated patients' cells respond ex vivo
efficacy.quote: CEP-18770 induces apoptotic cell death in multiple myeloma (MM) cell lines and in primary purified CD138-positive explant cultures from untreated and bortezomib-treated MM patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The explant result is pooled across patients, not a per-patient prediction; the same system carried oprozomib (Chauhan 2010, doi 10.1182/blood-2010-04-276626) and ixazomib (Chauhan 2011, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0476).
efficacy.population: CD138+ cells from untreated and bortezomib-treated MM patients
efficacy.judgement: Opened at first use (Piva 2008, epub 2007-12-05). Patient-level track: the system's claim is that cells from bortezomib-exposed or bortezomib-resistant patients still die on a member drug, i.e. which patients respond, not whether the class works. Separate from the cell-line xenograft tracks: different material, different prediction.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived primary CD138+ myeloma cells ex vivo, including cells from bortezomib-treated or bortezomib-resistant patients (Piva 2008; Chauhan 2010, 2011)
efficacy.note: Single-agent ixazomib gave PRs in the bortezomib-relapsed (3/10) and relapsed-refractory (2/11) expansion cohorts, as bortezomib-resistant patient cells ex vivo predicted.
efficacy.short: Responses after bortezomib, as ex vivo predicted
efficacy.quote: Responses were seen across the expansion cohorts, including 2, 3, 1, and 2 PRs in the relapsed and refractory, bortezomib-relapsed, PI-naive, and prior carfilzomib cohorts, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via the publisher page. Cohorts of 10-11 patients; no bortezomib-refractory cohort is reported, response was a secondary endpoint of a safety-primary phase 1, and the ex-vivo data were pooled across patients, so the match is direction only.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex vivo apoptosis in bortezomib-resistant patient cells (Chauhan 2011) vs PR rate in the bortezomib-relapsed cohort (3/10); no common scale
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, weekly single-agent ixazomib expansion cohorts by prior bortezomib/carfilzomib exposure (NCT00963820)

patient_trials.quote: Among 55 response-evaluable patients, 15% achieved partial response or better (76% stable disease or better).
In phase II, ORRs in 95 response-eligible multiple myeloma patients were 41.0%, 28.1%, and 25.0% in the 2/7, 240/300-mg/day; 5/14, 150/180-mg/day; and 5/14, 240-mg/day cohorts, respectively.
At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).

efficacy.reason: Responses after bortezomib, as ex vivo predicted
efficacy.judgement: Scored same rather than untested because Kumar 2014 reports responses by prior-bortezomib cohort, which is the patient-level question the ex-vivo system asked (Chauhan 2011: MLN2238 kills MM cells resistant to bortezomib therapy). Paired comparison: the trial paper only cites the model work. The FDA pharmacology review reproduces Chauhan 2011's ex-vivo cytotoxicity figure, so model_filed is true for ixazomib. endpoint_role null: ORR was a secondary endpoint of a safety-primary phase 1. Richardson 2014 (88% prior bortezomib, 15% ORR), oprozomib (Ghobrial 2019) and delanzomib (Vogl 2017, 9% PR) are same-direction and change no status; none reports a bortezomib-refractory subgroup. No source compares a patient's own ex-vivo result with that patient's clinical response to a member drug.

added_models.model: Berenson-lab SCID-hu LAGκ-1A (bortezomib-sensitive) and LAGκ-1B (bortezomib-resistant) patient-derived myeloma xenografts, dosed with delanzomib

efficacy.model: Berenson-lab SCID-hu LAGκ-1A (bortezomib-sensitive) and LAGκ-1B (bortezomib-resistant) patient-derived myeloma xenografts, dosed with delanzomib
efficacy.note: Oral single-agent CEP-18770 gave marked anti-MM effects in patient-derived LAGκ xenografts and, with bortezomib, delayed bortezomib-resistant tumours; no patient result yet.
efficacy.short: Oral single-agent activity in patient-derived xenografts
efficacy.quote: Single agent CEP-18770 PO also showed marked anti-MM effects in these xenograft models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The LAGκ-1A/-1B identity of the bortezomib-sensitive and bortezomib-resistant tumours comes from the Berenson-lab companion reports (ASH 2008 abstract 'Oral dosing of ... CEP-18770 ... in SCID-hu models'; Berenson 2012 Leuk Res, doi 10.1016/j.leukres.2012.07.018), not from this abstract.
efficacy.judgement: A separate track from delanzomib-mm-xenograft (Piva 2008, Cephalon cell-line xenografts): a different laboratory's patient-derived SCID-hu system with its own prediction (single-agent oral activity, retained activity against bortezomib-resistant disease in combination). Opened at the BJH epub (2009-12-01); the ASH 2008 abstract is earlier but was not verified beyond a search snippet.

efficacy.model: Berenson-lab SCID-hu LAGκ-1A (bortezomib-sensitive) and LAGκ-1B (bortezomib-resistant) patient-derived myeloma xenografts, dosed with delanzomib
efficacy.note: Single-agent delanzomib at the MTD gave 9% PR and development stopped, against marked single-agent activity in the LAGκ patient-derived xenografts.
efficacy.quote: At the MTD, 26 patients (55%) had stable disease and four (9%) had a partial response (PR).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT01023880 (ORR primary) terminated with no posted results. The combination prediction (delanzomib + dexamethasone/lenalidomide, Berenson 2012) reached NCT01348919: ORR 40% at the 1.8 mg/m2 MTD in a 5-patient cohort of 11 enrolled, results posted 2023-06-28, which changes no status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour growth inhibition vs single-agent PR rate (9%); not commensurable
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, single-agent delanzomib phase I/II (NCT01023880)

patient_trials.quote: Overall Response Rate (ORR) in Participants Treated at the (Maximum Tolerated Dose) MTD, as Assessed Using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) Criteria: 40 percentage of participants (95% CI 5.27 to 85.34)

efficacy.judgement: Same patient datum as the delanzomib-mm-xenograft contra, scored on its own track because the systems differ. Contra, not neg: the abstract gives no model effect size below a class bar. Dated 2017 (epub 2017-01-31); the trial posted no registry results. The LAGκ-1B bortezomib-resistant arm was only tested in combination with bortezomib in mice and never in patients, so the patient-level half of the prediction stays untested. The NCT01348919 patient_trials quote is the registry outcome-measure title and value, not prose.

added_models.model: Ixazomib population-PK model (NONMEM, 226 phase 1 patients) simulating exposure after fixed 4 mg versus BSA-based 2.23 mg/m2 dosing

dose.model: Ixazomib population-PK model (NONMEM, 226 phase 1 patients) simulating exposure after fixed 4 mg versus BSA-based 2.23 mg/m2 dosing
dose.note: PopPK of 226 phase 1 patients predicted fixed 4 mg gives the same AUC as 2.23 mg/m2 across body sizes; the phase 3 run at 4 mg had not read out.
dose.quote: there was no relationship between BSA and ixazomib clearance (the parameter that dictates total systemic exposure following fixed dosing)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The sponsor ran the analysis during phase 2 (FDA ClinPharmR: 'During Phase 2 evaluations, the sponsor's population PK analysis determined that body size does not significantly influence'); the 2015 paper is the earliest public record, so the track opens there.
dose.population: Phase 1 MM, lymphoma and solid-tumour patients on BSA-based ixazomib
dose.judgement: An in-silico dose-selection model under the brief's 'in-silico / QSP models used to choose doses'. Its stated target is exposure equivalence of fixed 4 mg to the 2.23 mg/m2 RP2D, which the phase 3 then tested.

dose.model: Ixazomib population-PK model (NONMEM, 226 phase 1 patients) simulating exposure after fixed 4 mg versus BSA-based 2.23 mg/m2 dosing
dose.note: FDA's popPK review of phase 3 data found body size does not move clearance; 4 mg fixed reached the predicted exposure and TOURMALINE-MM1 met its PFS primary.
dose.short: Fixed 4 mg reached target and worked
dose.quote: however it was not found to influence ixazomib central clearance or volume of distribution. This supports sponsor’s fixed dosing approach.
dose.confidence_note: Quote from the OCRed review text in the source bundle (sources/208462). Gupta 2017 (doi 10.1007/s40262-017-0526-4; 755 patients including TOURMALINE-MM1) confirms BSA 1.2-2.7 m2 is not a clearance covariate.
dose.magnitude_basis: simulated AUC after fixed 4 mg (Gupta 2015) vs popPK-estimated phase 3 exposure, BSA 1.2-2.7 m2 without a clearance effect
dose.population: Relapsed/refractory MM, TOURMALINE-MM1 (ixazomib 4 mg fixed, days 1, 8, 15)
dose.reason: Fixed 4 mg reached target and worked
dose.judgement: Dose rule 'reached, drug worked': the model's exposure target (AUC of the 2.23 mg/m2 RP2D) was reached at 4 mg fixed in the phase 3 population and the primary PFS was met (FDA SumR, on the mm1s-scid-xenograft efficacy track). comparison_stated true: the regulator's own popPK review puts model and patient data side by side. Dated 2015 with the review (approval 2015-11-20), before the registry posting (2016-01-27). No tolerability margin is stated by this model, so margin_stated false.

considered_not_added: iMycCα/Bcl-XL genetically engineered mouse and its DP54-Luc disseminated derivative (Lee 2011, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-0636; ixazomib): an immunocompetent model distinct from MM.1S/SCID, but its anti-tumour prediction (survival, IgG2a) has no patient comparison distinct from the MM.1S track, and its bone prediction ('only MLN2238 alleviated osteolytic bone disease') is matched only by a 2025 single-centre phase 2 of bone histomorphometry in 30 patients in remission (doi 10.1016/j.bone.2025.117660), which is neither an efficacy primary endpoint nor a PD readout of the target under the brief's cell definitions. Not scored; flagged for the checker if bone endpoints are later ruled admissible.

Bone-marrow-disseminated human myeloma mouse plus patient osteoclast/osteoprogenitor cultures (Garcia-Gomez 2014, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-13-1657; MLN2238 bone-anabolic prediction): same reason as above; no myeloma efficacy or engagement comparison.

Vk*MYC transgenic mouse: no member drug (ixazomib, delanzomib, oprozomib) found in any Vk*MYC report; 5TGM1/KaLwRij: no member-drug hits. Bortezomib and carfilzomib data on these models are non-members and set aside.

EMMA ex-vivo mathematical myeloma advisor (Silva 2017, doi 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-17-0502; 52 patients, 96% responder classification): full text contains no ixazomib or MLN entry, so no member-drug comparison.

3D tissue-engineered bone marrow (Alhallak 2021, doi 10.1038/s41598-021-98760-9; 19 RRMM patients, 89% regimen-level retrospective prediction): ixazomib appears only in the Css-calibration drug list; no ixazomib-containing regimen is identifiable in the text, so no member-drug patient comparison can be quoted.

'Direct to Drug' ex-vivo screen (Bonolo de Campos 2020, doi 10.1038/s41408-020-0320-7; ixazomib EC50 in 113 primary samples): clinical-outcome associations reported only for venetoclax and selinexor; no member-drug patient comparison.
Bortezomib-resistant human myeloma cell lines (ANBL-6.BR, MM.1S-BR; Chauhan 2010/2011, Kupperman 2010): in-vitro lines, not patient material; no patient comparison separate from the ex-vivo track.

Exposure-response logistic model for maintenance dose selection (Gupta 2016, doi 10.1007/s10637-016-0346-7; 3 mg to 4 mg titration for TOURMALINE-MM3/MM4): a different in-silico model whose patient side is newly diagnosed maintenance, outside the tile's relapsed/refractory population until rule question 3 is settled. PBPK CYP3A DDI model and the ORR-to-PFS model-based meta-analysis (Gupta 2019, doi 10.1002/cpt.1047): not dose-target or disease-model predictions.

Berenson 2012 LAGκ/RPMI8226 delanzomib + dexamethasone/lenalidomide xenografts (doi 10.1016/j.leukres.2012.07.018): same LAGκ system; its combination trial NCT01348919 (ORR 40% at MTD, 5 patients, results 2023-06-28) is recorded as patient_trials on the LAGκ track and changes no status.

Oprozomib in Waldenström macroglobulinaemia xenografts (Roccaro 2010): different disease. Solid-tumour and lymphoma phase 1 PD (Smith 2015): already the draft's engagement entry. Patient PBMC proteasome-inhibition assays: patient-side readouts, not a model system.
